clue.text: Broken sculpture

definitions.meaning: informally, something broken has gone kaput or smashed
a carved head-and-shoulders figure in stone or bronze

explanation.surface: A damaged statue in a gallery, described in two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: slang for wrecked, and a carved head-and-shoulders portrait.

clue.text: Flower that's flatter round top of calyx

indicators.note: round means the flattery phrase goes around the next piece

parts.note: to butter up is to flatter

indicators.note: top of picks the first letter of the following word in a down clue

explanation.surface: A flower described by a botanist, flattened round its calyx.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flatter' looks like an adjective (more flat) but is the verb; 'round' is the container signal and 'top of' takes a first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The yellow meadow ranunculus is a common wild bloom.

clue.text: Carpets woven in bands of colour

indicators.note: woven suggests threads interlaced, so the letters of carpets are rearranged

explanation.surface: Rugs woven in striped colours.
explanation.definitionFit: Light split by a prism shows rainbow ranges of hues, the plural of spectrum.

clue.text: Time in vehicles — and other vehicles?

indicators.note: the word in puts the time letter inside the vehicles word

parts.note: cars are vehicles

explanation.surface: A puzzle about one kind of vehicle containing time, and asking what else rolls along.
explanation.definitionFit: Wagons pulled by horses or pushed by hand are further types of wheeled transport, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Stop broadcasting comedian introducing uplifting poems

indicators.note: introducing means the comic takes the poems in among his letters

parts.note: a clown is a comedian

indicators.note: in a down clue uplifting means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: odes are poems

explanation.surface: A comic brings inspiring verse to a station going off air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uplifting' reads like praise for the poems, but in a down clue it turns them upwards; 'introducing' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The end of a station's transmissions for the day is the noun for ceasing to broadcast.

clue.text: Harsh treatment of king on trial by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it means the words are pronounced to give the answer

parts.note: R (rex, king) placed on ORDEAL (trial) gives R-ORDEAL, which in a British accent is said like the answer

explanation.surface: A monarch put on trial getting unfair treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: R stands for rex, Latin for king. R plus ORDEAL, said in a non-rhotic British accent, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An unfair deal or a bad bargain is an idiom for being treated badly.

clue.text: Starters of a spicy Latin American sauce served up

definitions.text: Starters of a spicy Latin American sauce served up

indicators.note: in a down clue served up means brought upwards, read from bottom to top
starters are the opening letters of each word that follows

explanation.surface: A spicy Latin American sauce served as an appetiser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starters of' takes ASLAS; 'served up' reverses it. The whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A piquant tomato-and-chilli dip from Latin American cooking is the dish described.

clue.text: Villain heading off for part of church

indicators.note: the villain word loses its heading, i.e. its first letter is taken off

parts.note: a knave is a rogue or villain

explanation.surface: A rogue making off from a church building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' removes the K from KNAVE.
explanation.definitionFit: The central body of a church, where the congregation sits, is a structural section of the building.

clue.text: Glint half put out resulting in darkness

indicators.note: put out means disturbed or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Half a gleam extinguished, leaving darkness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' shuffles GLINT HALF. It looks like extinguishing a light.
explanation.definitionFit: Dusk, when daylight ends, is the onset of dark.

clue.text: See a large elk get lost!

parts.note: V is short for vide, Latin for see
the moose is the large North American elk

explanation.surface: A warning to watch a big elk wander off.
explanation.walkthrough: V for 'vide' (see) is the reference-book abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A slang command to clear off or leave quickly.

clue.text: Broken leg woman athlete will get in sport with posh boys

indicators.note: the three words are broken up and their letters rebuilt into a new order

explanation.surface: An injured female runner still takes part in a game alongside public schoolboys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broken' shuffles LEG WOMAN ATHLETE. The Eton wall game is a muddy, rarely scored football-like game played only at Eton College, the elite English boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: This peculiar game is played by pupils of Eton, the archetypal school for privileged boys.

clue.text: Access space by bay perhaps

parts.note: an en is a printer's unit of space
the bay laurel is an example of a tree

explanation.surface: Getting into a parking space next to a loading bay.
explanation.walkthrough: The bay is the laurel tree, not a parking bay; 'perhaps' marks it as one example of a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Entry or the right of admission into a place or society is a formal synonym for access.

clue.text: Former partner with case making excessive demand

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner
a legal case is an action in court

explanation.surface: An ex-spouse bringing a lawsuit and asking far too much.
explanation.definitionFit: The act of extorting or demanding payment harshly is the formal sense of this noun.

clue.text: Drawing cleaner fuel

definitions.note: a sketch made with burnt-wood sticks is itself called by this name

parts.note: a char is a British cleaning woman, short for charwoman
coal is a fuel

explanation.surface: Choosing a cleaner kind of fuel to draw on.
explanation.walkthrough: A char is a British word for a cleaning lady. 'Drawing' looks like a verb (drawing fuel) but is a noun for a sketch.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist's sketch done in burnt-wood sticks is named after its medium.

clue.text: Assign new posts as revolutionary fresh fuel

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning things over, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Allocating jobs as if fresh fuel were some radical cause.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabinet change, moving ministers to different roles, is the political term for reallocating jobs.

clue.text: Adult in Switzerland rented house

parts.note: CH is the international vehicle code for Switzerland
A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult
let means rented out

explanation.surface: A grown-up renting a home in the Alps.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden Swiss-style dwelling or holiday cottage is a type of residence.

clue.text: Person in charge, a live wire maybe

definitions.meaning: a leader, as of an orchestra or a bus
a material carrying electric current, such as a live wire

explanation.surface: An energetic boss described two ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'live wire' seems to mean a lively person, but it is literally a wire carrying current.
explanation.definitionFit: Orchestra leaders bear this title, and so do materials that transmit electricity.

clue.text: What shoplifter does to assess the situation

definitions.meaning: a shoplifter literally removes goods, the shop's inventory
to review one's position before acting

explanation.surface: A thief weighing up their next move in a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for pausing to evaluate, read literally as making off with merchandise.

clue.text: Standards applied to cleric

parts.note: pars are standard levels, as in up to par
on means placed upon or applied to

explanation.surface: Rules being enforced on a churchman.
explanation.definitionFit: A vicar or rector, especially a parish priest, is a member of the clergy.

clue.text: Help carrying flightless bird for fool

indicators.note: carrying means the help word holds the bird inside it

parts.note: aid means help
the rhea is a flightless South American bird

explanation.surface: A dim helper lugging an ostrich-like bird around.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for an empty-headed, silly person.

clue.text: Second free product taken on beach holiday?

parts.note: to unblock is to free or clear

explanation.surface: A second free gift to pack for a seaside break.
explanation.definitionFit: Sun cream that screens out UV rays is an item packed for seaside trips; the question mark marks the definition by example.

clue.text: Abstract calculation carried out by woman

parts.note: a sum is a calculation
Mary is a woman's name

explanation.surface: Some theoretical arithmetic done by a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abstract' looks like an adjective but is the noun meaning a précis.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief synopsis of a paper is called its abstract.

clue.text: I'm a bank that's put up folding stuff

indicators.note: in a down clue put up means read upwards, so the letters run in reverse

parts.note: Giro, the Girobank, was a British bank

explanation.surface: A bank boasting about its banknotes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' reverses IM A GIRO. 'Folding stuff' is slang for paper money, but here it is paper-folding art.
explanation.definitionFit: The Japanese craft of shaping paper by creasing it is literally a folding pastime.

clue.text: Doctor upset carrying hooligan by a carriage

indicators.note: carrying means the doctor letters hold the other pieces inside them
upset in a clue means turned over, so the doctor letters run backwards

parts.note: MB is a medical degree, Bachelor of Medicine, so a doctor
a rough is a rowdy or hooligan

explanation.surface: An angry doctor taking a thug for a ride in a carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' sounds like an angry doctor but turns the medical degree backwards; 'carrying' makes it a container round the hooligan and A.
explanation.definitionFit: A light four-wheeled horse-drawn closed vehicle, named after Lord Brougham, is a kind of carriage.

clue.text: Make plans to steal lead from roof?

indicators.note: steal lead from means the first letter of the roof word is removed

parts.note: thatch is a roof of straw or reeds

explanation.surface: Plotting to strip lead off a roof.
explanation.walkthrough: Stealing lead from roofs is a real crime, but here 'lead' is the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To devise a plot or scheme, as one hatches a plan.

clue.text: Lingerie comes back to life apparently

definitions.meaning: read playfully as ..., reversing a death

explanation.surface: Underwear that seems to resurrect itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A colloquial word for underclothes, and also a joke reading as the opposite of perishing.

clue.text: Betook meat feast, cooked, and large fruit

indicators.note: cooked suggests the three words are prepared afresh into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone heads off to a carnivore's banquet with a large fruit on the side.
explanation.definitionFit: This big, fleshy variety of the salad plant is botanically a fruit.

clue.text: Regularly indulge, shunning work

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of the next word, starting from its first

explanation.surface: Someone habitually treating themselves instead of working.
explanation.definitionFit: Avoiding labour describes someone lazy or inactive.

clue.text: Historical novelist greeting the queen

parts.note: hey is an informal greeting
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the queen's cipher

explanation.surface: A writer of period fiction saying hello to the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Georgette of that surname wrote Regency romances and other historical fiction.

clue.text: Arrest devil?

definitions.meaning: to pinch or detain a suspect, in British slang

explanation.surface: Detaining the Devil himself.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for to arrest, and the short form of Old Nick, a name for the devil.
